name: South Miami City Commission

meetings.pattern: First and third Tuesday of most months, 7:00 p.m., Commission Chambers, City Hall, 6130 Sunset Drive, with Zoom participation (chambers open 6:30 p.m. for in-person comment). Charter Art. II Sec. 5C requires at least two meetings a month generally and at least one a month from Nov 1 to Jan 31 and Jun 1 to Aug 31.

schedule.note: First budget hearing, tentative millage and budget (FY2027 budget schedule)
Final budget hearing and regular meeting per the budget schedule; the schedule's layout also shows a Sept 20 line, so confirm the adoption date against the Granicus agenda
City Commission Meeting; also the runoff date if the Nov 3 election ties

phases.name: Proposed budget and workshop
phases.decides: Manager submits the proposed budget July 1 (charter Art. IV Sec. 2 requires it 60 days before the fiscal year); Commission budget workshop July 15 at 4:00 p.m.; proposed millage resolution July 21.

phases.name: September budget hearings
phases.decides: First hearing Sept 8 at 5:01 p.m. sets the tentative millage and budget; the final hearing adopts both by three affirmative votes before the fiscal year starts (charter Art. IV Sec. 2).

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: Fiscal year runs October 1 through September 30 (same as Miami-Dade County per charter Art. IV Sec. 1).

phases.name: Candidate qualifying for the 2026 general election
phases.decides: Who appears on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot for Mayor, Commissioner Group I and Commissioner Group IV. 9:00 a.m. July 27 to 5:00 p.m. Aug 7 by appointment with the City Clerk.

phases.name: Municipal general and special election
phases.decides: Mayor (Javier E. Fernandez, unopposed), Group I (Steve Calle, unopposed), Group IV (Lisa Bonich, unopposed), plus four charter questions (franchise definition, online ordinance notices, purchasing policy, vacancy special-election timing). Starting with this election the Mayor and these commissioners serve four-year terms (charter Art. V Sec. 2A). Runoff only on a tie, Dec 1, 2026.

levers.how: Speak at public remarks or a public hearing in person at City Hall (chambers open 6:30 p.m.) or on Zoom (zoom.us/j/3056636338; phone +1-786-635-1003). Raise your virtual hand (*9 by phone) only when the Mayor calls for hands; use your real name on Zoom or you may not be called.
levers.rules: Three minutes per speaker. No advance sign-up. Members of the public, applicants and their representatives may speak.

levers.how: No written comment procedure is posted in the meeting notice. The Clerk's office (CityClerk@SoMiFL.gov, 305-663-6340) is the posted contact.
Mayor and Commission directory on the city site; City Hall 305-663-6330.
Submit through the Clerk's public records request page.

Charter Art. V Sec. 6A(1): qualified voters may propose an ordinance by petition signed by at least 15 percent of registered voters at the last regular city election; if the Commission does not adopt it unchanged it goes to the voters. Not allowed for the budget, capital program, appropriations, tax levies or salaries.

Charter Art. V Sec. 6A(2): qualified voters may require the Commission to reconsider an adopted ordinance; the petition must be filed within 30 days and suspends the ordinance. Same subject exclusions as initiative. Charter amendments follow the county Home Rule Charter and state law (Art. VI Sec. 7).
levers.rules: 15 percent of registered voters; file within 30 days of adoption
levers.deadline: 30 days after the ordinance is adopted

levers.how: Charter Art. V Sec. 6H: a Commission member may be recalled as provided by state law (F.S. 100.361).

Schedule an appointment with the City Clerk (305-663-6340, nkenga.payne@somifl.gov) and file during the posted window. Charter Art. V Sec. 2D bars anyone who would serve nine years or more as Mayor or Commissioner.
levers.rules: Four-year terms starting with 2026; Vice Mayor is the commissioner with the most votes (Art. II Sec. 2)
levers.deadline: 5:00 p.m. on the last day of qualifying

levers.how: City elections are held in even years on the national general election day. Registration closed Oct 5, 2026; early voting Oct 19 to Nov 1; vote-by-mail requests by 5 p.m. Oct 22.

elections.terms: Mayor and four commissioners (Groups I to IV). Beginning with the 2026 election the Mayor and two commissioners (Groups I and IV) serve four years; the other two groups are elected in 2028. Term limit: no one may appear on the ballot who would serve nine or more years.
